keyTerms.definition: Answers for lesson 02b, kept separate from the lesson file.
The version used for all computed numbers, in float64.

recall.question: What grounds the numbers in these answer keys?
recall.answer: All numbers were computed 2026-10-06 with numpy 1.26.4 in float64.

keyTerms.definition: The f-divergence: expectation under q of f(p/q), with f convex and f(1) = 0.
The normalization that both KL and TV satisfy at t = 1.

recall.question: How do KL and TV both satisfy f(1) = 0?
recall.answer: KL gives 1 times log2(1) = 0 and TV gives |1-1|/2 = 0.

keyTerms.definition: The Jensen-Shannon divergence, computed here as 0.0667 bits.
The computed JS value for the given r and q.

recall.question: What is the computed JS value?

keyTerms.definition: The max over T: function optimization replacing the exact divergence.
The min over q: moving the model toward the data.

recall.question: What do the max over T and min over q each do?
recall.answer: The max over T is the variational step replacing the exact divergence; the min over q moves the model toward the data.

keyTerms.definition: The restricted class whose inner max is 0 against a true 0.2651 bits.
The shortfall when the witness class cannot approach T*.

recall.question: Why does the constant witness class give the wrong answer?
recall.answer: Its inner max is 0 but the true divergence is 0.2651 bits; the class cannot approach T*.

keyTerms.definition: The three weights summing to 1 in the n = 3 case.
The base Jensen step, used twice to build the n = 3 case.

recall.question: How is the n = 3 Jensen case proved?
recall.answer: By rewriting the mixture and applying the two-point case twice.

keyTerms.definition: The inequality f(E) <= E[f], which fails in the counterexample.
The violated condition: the chord dips below the graph.

recall.question: Which condition is violated in the E06 counterexample?
recall.answer: Convexity of f: for f(x) = x^3 - 3x the chord dips below the graph, so f(E) <= E[f] fails.

keyTerms.definition: The sup_t (s t - f(t)) form whose pointwise sup over T recovers f(r).
Claims resting on titles alone, with no transcript inspected.

recall.question: Why do the source claims stay title-level?
recall.answer: No transcript was inspected, so any claim about lecture content is PENDING; only titles were seen.

recall.question: What would promote a row to source-confirmed?
recall.answer: An inspected transcript or slide deck with a timestamp or page anchor showing the formula.
